Rules for participation in SUP adventures
Please read the rules carefully before booking. By confirming a booking, the participant agrees to comply with safety requirements, follow the route, and use the provided equipment responsibly.
Participation is permitted for persons who have read the rules, completed the safety briefing, and confirmed their agreement with the conditions.
The participant must follow the instructions of the organizer or instructor throughout the entire SUP trip.
The organizer has the right to refuse a participant access to the route or end the trip early if the participant violates the rules or creates a danger to themselves or others.
The maximum number of participants in one group is 4 people.
The participant must inform the organizer of any circumstances that may affect their safety on the water.
During the SUP trip, the participant must:
wear a properly fastened life jacket at all times;
attach the safety leash to their leg and not remove it without the organizer's permission;
use the SUP board only for its intended purpose;
not move away from the group without permission;
keep a safe distance from boats, motorboats, bridges, rocks, supports, and other obstacles;
go ashore only at designated places;
immediately inform the organizer about equipment damage, worsening health, or a dangerous situation;
follow the organizer's instructions if the weather changes or an emergency occurs.
During the SUP trip, it is prohibited to:
be under the influence of alcohol, drugs, or other intoxicating substances;
consume alcohol or prohibited substances before entering the water or during the route;
intentionally overturn other participants' SUP boards;
push other participants into the water;
jump from a SUP board in unknown or unapproved locations;
approach motorboats or other watercraft too closely;
hand the equipment over to third parties;
use sharp objects, open flames, or other items that may damage the board;
drag the SUP board over stones, asphalt, concrete surfaces, or sharp objects;
leave the agreed route without the organizer's permission.
Children under 7 years of age are not permitted on SUP routes.

The organizer may set additional age restrictions depending on the route, weather, current, and the child's physical fitness.

The participant must inspect the equipment before entering the water and immediately report any detected damage or defects.
Starting to use the equipment means that the participant has accepted it in visibly serviceable condition unless otherwise recorded before the start.
From the moment the equipment is handed over until it is returned, the participant must:
not hand it over to other persons;
return it with the same complete set of items;
The participant is responsible for loss of or damage to the equipment if it occurred:
due to violation of these rules;
due to use for purposes other than intended;
due to handing the equipment over to a third party;
due to leaving the equipment unattended;
due to leaving the agreed route without permission.
In the event of damage, the participant reimburses the documented cost of repair.
If repair is impossible or economically unreasonable, the participant reimburses the cost of replacing the damaged or lost equipment with equivalent equipment.
The participant is not responsible for:
damage caused by the organizer's actions;
damage that occurred despite proper use and compliance with all instructions.
Where possible, the fact and nature of the damage are recorded with photographs or video.

Providing a dry bag does not guarantee complete protection of belongings from water. Before the route begins, the participant must personally check that it is properly closed.

exposure to sun, wind, and temperature;
Acceptance of these rules does not release the organizer from liability that, under applicable law, cannot be transferred to the participant.
In case of danger, the participant must:
Do not leave the SUP board unless the organizer gives a different instruction.
Hold on to the board or another floating device.
Help others only when doing so does not create additional danger.
The organizer may take photos and videos during the route.
Consent to publish materials on social media or the website must be provided separately during booking.
Refusal to allow publication of photographs does not affect the ability to participate.
Acceptance of the rules during booking

On the booking page, participants must confirm that they have read the rules. For children to participate, consent from a parent or legal guardian is additionally required. Permission to use photos and videos remains optional.
